# Citation

Dawadi et al. (2025). *From bench to bytes: a practical guide to RNA
sequencing data analysis*. Frontiers in Genetics 16:1697922. DOI:
10.3389/fgene.2025.1697922.

# One-Sentence Summary

A decision-oriented guide to selecting and interpreting RNA-seq processing and
statistical-analysis steps, written for researchers moving from experimental
RNA work into computational analysis.

# Scope for simitall

Use as workflow context for clearly separating read generation, QC,
alignment/quantification, count matrices, differential expression, and
biological interpretation. It supports asking users for the missing design and
provenance information before code is proposed.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- RNA-seq workflows require explicit file-format and processing provenance.
- Tool selection depends on the question, data type, reference quality, and
  compute constraints; no single default applies to every study.
- Simulated read truth and simulated count truth should remain distinguishable.

# Limitations and Guardrails

This review is guidance, not a benchmark establishing that one tool is best.
Use primary method papers and official manuals for package-specific behavior.
